findings.finding: The opening heroine is off-model, wears the wrong wardrobe including knee-high socks, and is rendered in the wrong style. The scene is not the approved SUNNYVAiLE.
The candidate behaves predominantly as a slideshow. Camera movement, zoom or holding a generated still is not meaningful scene animation and does not satisfy the animation standard.

The woman shown is not the approved heroine. The surrounding men and other people are invented, unidentified characters with no established role in the scene. A generic generated crowd cannot substitute for approved heroine and town-character canon.

The heroine switches into an episode-specific outfit instead of maintaining the locked Trailer wardrobe. Every heroine occurrence must be checked, not only the seven frames named by the prior replacement batch.
The film uses a retired SUNNYVAiLE town map. The current approved geography/map must replace it; an obsolete map cannot be repaired cosmetically or treated as close enough.

The scene invents a human tour-guide character and places her over another obsolete/noncanonical town map. The tour-tracking explanation must use the current approved tour system and current SUNNYVAiLE geography without inventing a person who does not exist in canon.

The frame shows JoJo in Blend & Snap, which is her established workplace, but the trailer never introduces her or explains her role. This occurrence can remain only if the consolidated trailer makes the character legible without requiring prior canon knowledge.

The trailer does not explain that the heroine changes from her corporate look into a Rewind Era outfit when she enters SUNNYVAiLE, and it does not name or explain the Rewind Era. The transformation therefore reads as unexplained outfit inconsistency rather than an intentional story beat.

The transformation first reveals the Episode 4 yellow-plaid outfit and then switches to the intended Trailer outfit. The accepted sequence must transition directly from the established corporate look to one approved Trailer/Rewind Era look without flashing any episode-specific wardrobe.

The film uses an old, retired LAiDIES wordmark that must never be reused. The successor must use the exact current approved animated wordmark identity and checksum. Ali approved the electric burst background treatment at this beat; retain that background while replacing only the prohibited identity treatment.

The Episode 1 promo card and recorded announcement use the retired title 'On Wednesdays We Use AI.' The current approved title is 'On Wednesdays We Do AI.' Retain the comic promo-card concept only after both the visible title and spoken/captioned title are corrected to the current canon.
Hedy and the other MAiVENS are shown as SUNNYVAiLE town characters. The established boundary forbids this treatment.
Captions alter approved capitalization when names or terms are spelled aloud. Captions must preserve the exact approved LAiDIES spelling and casing.

The town-anthem outro starts without any visual or spoken handoff identifying what is about to play, so it feels random. The picture then cycles through disconnected images reused from the trailer instead of a coherent song-specific outro sequence, the ornate postcard frame is visually rejected, and the film ends abruptly without a professionally resolved final beat. Build a deliberate anthem introduction, one narration/music-relevant visual sequence, an approved clean postcard/end-card treatment and a finished audio/visual landing.

The Control Room player used native default captions over the picture instead of the required caption band below it. The inbox player was corrected; public watch.html already used the below-picture treatment.
